title: How a 153-Pound Fish Was Caught on 2-Pound Line
description:
How do you land a 153-pound fish on line rated for 2 pounds?
In 2025 an angler on Lake Livingston, Texas, landed a 153-pound alligator gar on line rated for just 2 pounds. How? In the water, a fish is about as dense as water, so it weighs almost nothing: the line only has to handle its pull, not its weight. And the reel's drag lets line slip out before it can snap. The fish tires itself out. Just never lift it by the line.

Source: Outdoor Life, April 2025 (reported as a pending IGFA line-class world record). The gar in the video is our own 3D model.

How it's made: original 3D characters and scenes, animated by us; the tension gauge follows a simple drag model. The voices are AI voices (ElevenLabs).

Counterphysical: fishing physics that breaks your intuition.
